quotes.speaker: Mychal Thompson
quotes.summary_phrase: Teaching young athletes to prioritize personal accountability over blaming teammates
quotes.excerpt: It's a very difficult thing to teach kids to recognize to own their own mistakes.
quotes.quote: I'm working right now with my sons about accountability. When you played a game and you made some mistakes, if I ask you what happened, you're going to point out your teammate's mistake. It's a very difficult thing to teach kids to recognize to own their own mistakes, not blame their teammates and to focus on that. It's constant communication and there might be some progress and then two steps back. I always said, what else could you do to affect the game? Are you playing better defense? Take care of your assignment and your role and star in that role and good things will happen around you. Taking accountability is something you're taught at a young age, and we all fail at it, adults as well.

quotes.speaker: Mychal Thompson
quotes.summary_phrase: Implementing a twenty-four hour rule for post-game parent communication
quotes.excerpt: You cannot come up and have this conversation. You have the 24 hour rule.
quotes.quote: When I was a coach, we had rules and I would set those rules up with parents. After a tournament or after a game if you're upset, you cannot come talk to me. You have the 24 hour rule. You can call me and email me in 24 hours and we can set up a time. I also had a rule that when you get in that car with your kid driving home from the game, try to talk about something else. Let your kids drive the conversation, but don't talk about other mistakes that other people made. It's just not the right way to do it.

quotes.speaker: Mychal Thompson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mychal Thompson discusses the Clippers' response to the NBA investigation
quotes.excerpt: we vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation.
quotes.quote: We vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence. What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner Silver set at the start of the investigation to ensure its fairness and accuracy. For the past year, we cooperated fully and in good faith. We will now fight just as hard to demonstrate our innocence. We intend to vigorously challenge these findings and penalties through every avenue available to us and look forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process.

quotes.speaker: Mychal Thompson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mychal Thompson comments on Steve Ballmer's statement
quotes.excerpt: Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is complying with the NBA's punishments of the franchise for salary cap circumvention.
quotes.quote: Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is complying with the NBA's punishments of the franchise for salary cap circumvention, deciding not to pursue any legal action. Statement from Ballmer. This has been a very difficult time for everybody associated with the Clippers and for that, I have sincere regrets. I want to apologize to our fans, employees and my fellow NBA team owners for the distraction and distress this matter has caused, for which I accept responsibility as principal owner. We are committing to put this chapter behind us. We have communicated to the NBA that we are complying with the penalties assessed by the league, have paid the fine and are moving forward. While there are still disagreements concerning the findings in the report, this is not where I want to focus. Team owners should support, not distract.

quotes.speaker: Mychal Thompson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mychal Thompson praises Caitlin Clark's impact on women's basketball
quotes.excerpt: I have been fascinated about how much the WNBA and women's basketball just likes Caitlin Clark.
quotes.quote: I have been fascinated about how much the WNBA and women's basketball just likes Caitlin Clark and refuses to acknowledge a greatness and her impact on the game. Do you see where she was not even starting for Team USA in the World Cup and the World Cup and she just happens to be the most prolific guard in the WNBA combining scoring and assists. She's setting records. She combines the most points of any backcourt player in the WNBA history, but yet she cannot start for Team USA. This this is the strangest reaction to a superstar in a league in sports history.

quotes.speaker: Mychal Thompson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mychal Thompson discusses the WNBA's reaction to Caitlin Clark
quotes.excerpt: she is the straw that stirs the drink.
quotes.quote: It is crazy. Her and Angel Reese, we sometimes be criticize Angel Reese and we critique her and laugh at her game sometimes, but one thing that young lady can do is rebound and she played great defense and she actually scored some baskets in Team USA. And whenever she and Caitlin were on the floor, they were flowing, they were in sync. They look like Malone and Stockton and they were leading the team, but then Carol Lawson and the old veterans on the team are jealous or envious and they would put them on the bench and not play them, even though they were the best one-two punch for Team USA. It is strange to see how petty the WNBA is when it comes to the young stars. It's weird. No, these are the same people who are involved in the WNBA. It's the same, it's the same sort of response or reaction. They just do not want to let this woman take over women's basketball because they really believe it's more than just Caitlin Clark that generates all this worldwide interest and they don't realize it is her and her alone. Yes, there are other stars in the league, there are other good, there are all other WNBA players, no question about it, but she is the straw that stirs the drink.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver
quotes.summary_phrase: Ben Golliver on the Kawhi Leonard trade and the Clippers' future

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Trudell

text_blocks.speaker: Ben Golliver
text_blocks.text: Kawhi Leonard will be a Toronto Raptor, Brandon Ingram, Grady Dick will be Los Angeles Clippers. Those teams are now able to go into media day with certainty about their direction. It took longer than anybody wanted, but I think it actually resolved more cleanly than any of us could have ever hoped for. And I got to tip my hat to Adam Silver.

quotes.speaker: Ben Golliver

text_blocks.speaker: Ben Golliver
text_blocks.text: How many teams really want to be in the Kawhi Leonard business, right? I mean, obviously Toronto did, but I don't know what his trade market looked like this summer and he has not signed that next contract yet. And so you start to wonder like, how much of a net positive really was Adam Silver in this scenario? Anybody could have gotten Kawhi Leonard a max contract in 2019, right? But the real work goes in when Kawhi Leonard's now in his mid-30s. He hasn't done anything in the playoffs in five years, right? I mean, there's been collapse after collapse after collapse for the Clippers when they have made the playoffs. I mean, this year the collapse came early in the play-in tournament. And so now the real work begins for Kawhi Leonard's agent, trying to get him this next contract, this big money.
